title: Paramount Completes $81 Billion Warner Bros. Takeover
paragraphs: Paramount has completed its $81 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, bringing together two of Hollywood's oldest and most famous studios under a single company.

The deal closed on Tuesday, October 6. The combined company is now called Skydance. Including debt, the total value of the acquisition is nearly $111 billion. Paramount paid $31 per share for Warner Bros. Discovery.

The new company owns a huge range of well-known brands. These include the streaming services HBO Max and Paramount+, the news networks CNN and CBS, and famous films such as "Harry Potter," "Top Gun" and "The Godfather." The company plans to combine its streaming services and expects to save about $6 billion in costs.

The company is led by billionaire David Ellison, who called the day "historic." Ynon Kreiz, the former head of the toy company Mattel, has been named co-CEO and will manage day-to-day operations. Ellison's company, Skydance, bought Paramount for $8 billion last year before turning its attention to Warner.

The path to the deal was complicated. In December, Warner initially agreed to a deal with Netflix. Paramount then made a hostile bid and later raised its offer, causing Netflix to withdraw. Warner shareholders approved the merger with Paramount in April.

The merger also faced strong opposition. Thousands of Hollywood professionals, including actors Jane Fonda and Mark Ruffalo, signed an open letter against it, warning that it could lead to fewer jobs. In July, 12 Democratic state attorneys general sued to block the deal, as did the Writers Guild of America. In September, however, a judge approved settlements in which the company agreed to increase film production in the US, support workers who lose their jobs, and create a board to protect editorial independence at CNN and CBS.

Critics say these measures are too weak. Concerns have also been raised because President Donald Trump, a longtime ally of the Ellison family, has repeatedly criticized CNN's reporting. The company has kept Mark Thompson as CNN's editor-in-chief, and Ellison has said the network's editorial independence will be maintained.
